explanation:
I found no Mathlib declaration matching this theorem. It is specific to the library. It says that a level automorphism of the modular-curve function field K preserves the Gauss valuation ring W₀ if and only if the reduction of ε mod q fixes the line at infinity. Every main notion in the statement is the library's own definition: `levelAutBar`, `redQ`, `lineInfty`, `xHFunctionField`, `laurentBaseChange`, `jqModC`, `IsLevelAutAt` and `fieldBar`. Mathlib has no theory of modular-curve function fields as Laurent-series subfields, and no level-structure automorphisms acting on them.

The proof does not apply a single Mathlib lemma. It combines several of the library's own results (`comap_levelAutBar_eq_of_redQ_smul_lineInfty_eq`, `levelAutBar_mul`, `coe_levelAutBar_apply_eq_qExpand_sq_of_dvd_of_mem_laurentBaseChange_gamma0`, `comap_gauss_ne_of_coe_apply_eq_qExpand_sq_jqModC`) with a matrix construction. Its only Mathlib ingredients are generic: `ValuationSubring.mem_comap`, the `ZMod` casts and the `SpecialLinearGroup` coercion lemmas.

I did not search Mathlib, because none of these constants exist there.
